instruction: Examine the book reading record spreadsheet on the desktop. Using https://howlongtoread.com/ as reference, identify the book with the fastest reading pace (words per day) and write its title in book_list_result.docx.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully examined the book reading spreadsheet, visited howlongtoread.com to look up word counts for each book, calculated words per day, identified 'Out of the Silent Planet' as having the slowest reading pace, and wrote the title to book_list_result.docx.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open and read spreadsheets in LibreOffice Calc, navigate to external websites in Chrome, look up book information, perform calculations (words/day), open and type in LibreOffice Writer documents, save files.
metadata.task_rationale: Flips the original task from slowest to fastest reading pace. Same workflow (spreadsheet analysis + howlongtoread.com lookup + docx writing) but different target. The Shining has an extremely high reading pace (24767 words/day) due to being read in only 6 days.
metadata.explanation: Custom getter reads the docx file from VM and extracts text. Metric checks if the text contains 'The Shining' (the book with the fastest reading pace at ~24767 words/day). Partial credit given for partial title matches.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads docx file from VM and extracts paragraph text, returning {'text': text} format.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': accesses expected.get('expected_title') directly from the rules dict.
Case-insensitive containment check is appropriate and robust for title matching.
Postconfig properly saves the document (Ctrl+S) before evaluation, ensuring the getter reads the latest content.
Data flow is consistent: getter returns {'text': ...}, metric reads result.get('text'), compares against expected_title.
Partial credit logic (word overlap at 0.5x weight) is reasonable for partial matches.

Minor concern: expected value 'The Shining' as fastest reading pace cannot be independently verified without access to the actual spreadsheet data, though the metadata rationale (24767 words/day in 6 days) is plausible.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider verifying the expected value 'The Shining' against the actual spreadsheet data to ensure correctness of the fastest reading pace calculation.
